subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What recurring types of problems show up in these incident tickets?

judge.implied_focus: Recurring problem type (thematic category of the incident) and its prevalence across tickets

per_column.name: problem_type
per_column.rationale: Directly infers a semantic category of the underlying problem from ticket text, realizing the focus of 'recurring types of problems' with a coherent, data-inferable set of values (VPN, Email, Database, etc.).

per_column.name: problem_frequency_rank
per_column.rationale: Ranks each problem_type by observed frequency, adding a prevalence facet around the same focus. It is largely a deterministic derivative of the counts, but it does quantify recurrence, which is central to the query.

judge.rationale: Both columns centre tightly on one coherent, inferable focus -- the recurring problem type -- so focus_coherence is high. The focus is genuinely actionable: an analyst can prioritise VPN/Email/Database issues for root-cause work. However, structure_quality is only moderate: the second column (frequency_rank) is essentially a mechanical restatement of the aggregate counts of the first column rather than an independent analytical facet or predictor. A stronger structure would add differentiating attributes of the problem (e.g., inferred root-cause area, affected service, resolution pattern, recurrence over time), not just a rank of the same category. So the pair leans toward a single concept plus its restatement rather than a well-differentiated facet set.
